description.narrative:
In line with the Swedish strategy for Iraq Sida decided in 2019 to provide financial support to a media programme in Iraq that was run by Internews . The programme amounted to 32 000 000 SEK for a four year programme in the period of 2019-2022. In April 2023 the agreement was extended until 30 June 2024 with an expectation of enhancing the reach of some of the results of the programme and to integrate some of the lessons learned in from the evaluation of the programme implementation. In the 10 month extension Sida added 480 000 USD for the activities in 2023.
The goal of the Aswatouna" programme (our voices) is to empower women to participate equally as citizens and decision-makers by strengthening and expanding women's voices in Iraq. The project also contributes to Internews ongoing efforts globally to improve access to information as a root solution to enable women and men to make informed decisions, participate in dialogue and stand up for their rights. In the last year of the programme some small changes was made to the objectives of the programme. One new element concerned a focus on the working environment for journalists and to strengthen the resilience of women journalists to harassment and threats.
Strategic objectives for the programme are:
1. Increase the capacity of journalists and CSOs to produce high quality inclusive content which is gender-sensitive, amplifies womens voices, addresses womens issues and provides information which meets womens needs
2. Increase presence of womens voices in the media and public debate
3. Strengthen women journalists and CSO leaders resilience against and ability to protect themselves from gender-based digital attacks
4. Support womens empowerment by building their leadership opportunities in the media and information space
5. Inform and educate Iraqi women on their political and economic rights and the importance of womens political and economic participation.

Insatsen avser stöd till Internews projekt Aswatouna - Our Voices som syftar till att stärka och utöka kvinnors röster i Irak. Projektet kommer också att bidra till Internews pågående insatser globalt att förbättra tillgången till information som en grund för att göra det möjligt för kvinnor och män att fatta välgrundade beslut, delta i dialog och stå upp för sina rättigheter.
Projektet har följande mål:
- Öka kapaciteten hos journalister och organisationer i det civila samhället för att kunna producera innehåll av hög kvalitet som förstärker kvinnors röster, tar upp kvinnors frågor och ger information som möter kvinnors behov.
- Öka närvaron av kvinnor i media och i den offentliga debatten.
- Stärka kvinnliga journalister och CSO-ledares motståndskraft och förmåga att skydda sig mot könsrelaterade digitala attacker.
- Stödja kvinnors egenmakt genom att bygga upp deras möjligheter till ledarskap inom media och information.
- Informera och utbilda irakiska kvinnor om deras politiska och ekonomiska rättigheter samt vikten av kvinnors politiska och ekonomiska deltagande.
Sida avser att bidra med totalt 32 150 000 SEK under 2019-2021.

Internews Europe has applied to Sida for funding of 32 150 000 SEK to carry out the Aswatouna - Our Voices. Elevating and Amplifying Women's voices in Iraq during the period 2019-2021.
The goal of the intervention is to empower women to participate equally as citizens and decision-makers by strengthening and expanding women's voices in Iraq. The project will also contribute to Internews ongoing efforts globally to improve access to information as a root solution to enable women and men to make informed decisions, participate in dialogue and stand up for their rights

sector.narrative: Women’s rights organisations and movements, and government institutions

description.narrative:
In the 2022 report Internews stated that the Aswatouna I progamme has continued to give audiences increased access to high-quality, evidence-based information that is inclusive, relevant, and engaging. This was achieved through building the capacity of 45 journalists on gender-sensitive reporting, training 47 women journalists and university students on mobile journalism techniques and awarding 32 story production grants to encourage and enable journalists to produce innovative gender-sensitive content. Moreover, Aswatouna I increased the visibility and presence of women in the media.
Internews has also set up a new database of women journalists and experts on different topics that offer their assistance to media outlets who are looking for professionals with expertise on different topics. Aswatouna I furthermore supported four filmmakers in the production of films focused on unreported and/or under-reported women's stories. Holistic security and safety training for all participants strengthened their resilience against digital and physical attacks. And three regional advocacy outreach events fostered collaboration and cooperation between all relevant stakeholders, including citizens, local and national government representatives, along with media outlets and coalitions for civil society organistions.
In connection with the 2022 report Internews also presented an Outcome Harvesting evaluation report, which is a participatory evaluation method used for identifying, describing, and verifying the changes brought about by a project or initiative. The evaluation resulted in identifying 14 outcomes that can be contributed to the Aswatouna I program. The identified outcomes spread across various outcome levels, spanning from the individual to the public policy level. At the individual level, the identified outcomes were: • Increasing the capacity and skills of journalists and Women Human Rights Defender participants in terms of their understanding and practice in adhering to gender-sensitive reporting principles; • And improved their techniques and skills to protect themselves from and respond to digital and physical security threats, enabling them to apply safety measures to be able to carry out their work more securely; • And enabled the participants to produce more content that focuses on women issues that is gender sensitive in innovative ways. • And Increased participants understanding and skills in economic and political reporting.
At the organization level, the identified outcomes were: • Increased capacity of CSOs and partners in project management, budgeting, fundraising and advocacy.
Additionally, at the community and public policy level • the advocacy campaigns and coordination with universities and authorities resulted in decisions that economically supported women participants, mainstream media focusing and covering women issues. • the collaborations contributing to the potential integration of evidence-informed gender sensitive guidelines into government policies as well as introduction of a gender-sensitive reporting component to the media and journalism studies curriculum at universities across Iraq.
During 2023 Aswatouna II achieved among the results mentioned below Successfully trained 23 journalists and activists (10 men, 13 women) in environmental constructive journalism and digital security. Successfully trained 19 journalists (10 men, 9 women) in investigative journalism in collaboration with Awan Organisation. As a result, 10 investigative pieces were produced through an individualized mentorship process. Focus groups launching in depth discussions on themes such as: "What are the effects of the climate crisis on women and children, can you name some of them?" Answers are quoted below: * Skin burning and immunity weakening, and sickness. * School dropouts for children due to high temperature in some areas. * Malnutrition and early marriage of adolescent girls. * Economic hardship due to decrease in agricultural production which results in weakened agricultural related business and even daily consumption, which can lead to replacement too. * Immigration, which causes mental pressure once families are forced to immigrate from rural areas to cities. And there have bad living situations..
Twenty two (22) media outlets signed a memorandum of understanding (MOU) with Internews to publish produced content pieces and support the selection of journalists for Internews activities.
24 high quality investigative and solutions oriented content pieces produced and disseminated in more than 45 local and MENA region media outlets. Successfully completed the training program for 15 decision makers in media foundations (9 men, 6 women) on developing gender responsive policies and implementing a Code of Conduct to address sexual harassment in the media. This collaboration with Awan organisation led to the development of gender responsive policies & codes of conduct against sexual harassment in the media by 14 media outlets. The process involved in person training, working sessions, and mentorship tailored for media outlet managers and decision makers. In partnership with Awan Organisation one Guideline Manual under the title Guiding Manual on Sexual Harassment in Media Outlets was updated and published in Arabic language through local media outlets and the Internews Iraq web-page.
